criteria.title: Correct workflow layer

evidence.quote: **Phase:** STRUCTURE (information architecture and navigation only)

criteria.rationale: The response stays at IA/navigation and explicitly excludes code and visual implementation.

criteria.title: Mixed taxonomy detection

evidence.quote: Healthcare (industry), Enterprise (organization/audience), Getting Started (lifecycle) are siblings

criteria.rationale: It identifies all three supplied incompatible classification dimensions explicitly.

criteria.title: User-impact explanation

evidence.quote: Users cannot consistently predict what belongs under Solutions; onboarding is particularly misplaced

criteria.rationale: It connects the mixed taxonomy to predictability and orientation, labeling effects as hypotheses rather than measured confusion.

criteria.title: Content integrity

evidence.quote: 10/10 required entries explicitly mapped; zero intentional content deletions

criteria.rationale: The coverage matrix gives Monitor, Automate, Healthcare, Enterprise, Getting Started, Blog, Case Studies, Pricing, About and Contact/demo explicit destinations; the conditional demo route preserves Contact.

criteria.title: Evidence discipline

evidence.quote: No live website, analytics, competitor sites, user research, CMS inventory, or implementation was available or consulted.
`By organization` is a provisional taxonomy that should be renamed if the actual page proves otherwise.

criteria.rationale: No unsupported analytics/research/competitor results appear. New grouping labels and route assumptions are explicitly provisional, with validation conditions.

criteria.title: Grouping rationale

evidence.quote: Products = capability; Solutions explicitly separated by industry vs organization; Resources = content type; Getting Started = lifecycle

criteria.rationale: Every major group has a user question and membership rule. The nested Solutions headings explicitly separate industry and organization facets; lifecycle guidance is removed from that grouping.

criteria.title: Inventory-first behavior

evidence.quote: The action order is **Reuse → Extend → Variant → Compose → New**.

criteria.rationale: The mapping is grounded in all supplied component responsibilities before the new comparison responsibility is justified.

criteria.title: Existing component reuse

evidence.quote: Seven distinct existing component types are used:
No existing component API change or new variant is required based on the supplied requirements.

criteria.rationale: The section table explicitly reuses HeroSection, LogoWall, FeatureCard, MetricBand, CaseStudyFeature and CTASection; SectionHeader is optional composition.

criteria.title: New-component restraint

evidence.quote: None of the seven existing components owns a matrix of feature rows crossed with plan columns.
One generic new comparison component is therefore the smallest justified addition.

criteria.rationale: PlanComparisonTable is the sole proposed new component, with clear row/column semantics and a reason cards/metrics cannot cleanly substitute.

criteria.title: No page-specific duplicates

evidence.quote: Do not add `EnterpriseHero`, `EnterpriseFeatureCard`, `EnterpriseMetricBand`, `EnterpriseCaseStudy`, `EnterpriseLogoWall`, or `EnterpriseCTA`

criteria.rationale: It explicitly refuses page-named duplicates and avoids using an enterprise variant as a page identity tag.

criteria.title: Action rationale

evidence.quote: **Reuse**; **Compose** as a three-card group
**New**, with optional **Compose**

criteria.rationale: All seven sections receive explicit reuse/compose/new decisions and explanations tied to responsibilities. No unsubstantiated extensions or variants are introduced.

criteria.title: System implications

evidence.quote: Keep semantic table structure and enable horizontal scrolling if needed; preserve all feature values and labels.
**No token changes can be justified or verified.**

criteria.rationale: The comparison contract covers keyboard scrolling, header associations, complete values, zoom, focus and non-color availability; token changes remain evidence-gated.

criteria.title: Evidence integrity

evidence.quote: Analytics, user research and competitor evidence absent
No conversion uplift, performance improvement or accessibility conformance is claimed.

criteria.rationale: The evidence ledger preserves missing research, copy, metrics, routes, token values and implementation facts as unknown; numeric or user-study outcomes are not invented.

criteria.title: Audit before redesign

evidence.quote: ## 1. DISCOVER — project context and current-site audit
## 5. EXPLORE — bounded visual directions (same IA and wireframe)

criteria.rationale: Source-backed structural audit and IA/content mapping precede the bounded visual hypotheses; the output does not substitute styling for structural diagnosis.

criteria.title: IA consistency

evidence.quote: Split into Use Cases / Enterprise / Start Here

criteria.rationale: Kubernetes technical context, Enterprise audience and Start Here lifecycle no longer remain interchangeable siblings under Solutions. Product names and public Pricing stay reachable.

criteria.title: Content coverage

evidence.quote: All 13 required categories have destinations.
Do not delete unless equivalent tested form/path exists

criteria.rationale: Both the C01-C13 register and detailed disposition table account for all required content, including underlying contact form, proof, metrics, Docs and About. No category is silently removed.

criteria.title: Page hierarchy

evidence.quote: understand → select product/use case → verify proof → review buying information → request a demo
homepage hero **Explore products** = primary learning step and **Request demo** = secondary hero action

criteria.rationale: The homepage gives a coherent evaluation journey and distinguishes the persistent primary demo conversion from the hero's learning action and subordinate proof/pricing links. The rubric does not prescribe an exact hero CTA order.

criteria.title: Component governance

evidence.quote: The proposed page map creates **zero proven new component needs**.

criteria.rationale: The ten-component inventory and page/section mapping precede conditional new-component decisions. No new homepage component is authorized without an observed gap; page-specific copies and token proliferation are explicitly avoided.

criteria.title: Implementation discipline

evidence.quote: Keep implementation aligned with existing frontend stack; no migration proposed.
Implement semantic page structures and accurate text first, followed by responsive layout and styles in the existing stack

criteria.rationale: It preserves the existing stack, gives traceable content/route/component dependencies, and sequences structural implementation before visual refinement.

criteria.title: Validation discipline

evidence.quote: Keyboard traversal, focus, zoom/reflow, form error association, text alternatives, contrast, screen reader testing
Baseline-versus-proposed screenshots and functional/content regression log

criteria.rationale: The gate matrix and concrete acceptance checks separately cover evidence, IA/content parity, component reuse, responsive behavior, accessibility and regressions while explicitly marking actual tests unperformed.

non_scoring_observations: IA uses explicit nested industry/organization facets; their usefulness remains a stated hypothesis rather than empirical success
The B2B hero learning CTA differs from the illustrative expected artifact but preserves an explicit coherent conversion hierarchy; exact golden wording/order is not required
Length and additional visual hypotheses earn no bonus; only rubric behavior is scored
No rendered, research, accessibility-conformance or production outcome is established by this planning benchmark
